original_value: In modern society, air pollution is an important topic as this pollution exerts a critically bad influence on human health and the environment. Among air pollutants, Particulate Matter (PM2.5) consists of suspended particles with a diameter equal to or less than 2.5 μm. Sources of PM2.5 can be coal-fired power generation, smoke, or dusts. These suspended particles in the air can damage the respiratory and cardiovascular systems of the human body, which may further lead to other diseases such as asthma, lung cancer, or cardiovascular diseases. To monitor and estimate the PM2.5 concentration, Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) are combined and applied to the PM2.5 forecasting system. To compare the overall performance of each algorithm, four measurement indexes, Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) Pearson correlation coefficient and Index of Agreement (IA) are applied to the experiments in this paper. Compared with other machine learning methods, the experimental results showed that the forecasting accuracy of the proposed CNN-LSTM model (APNet) is verified to be the highest in this paper. For the CNN-LSTM model, its feasibility and practicability to forecast the PM2.5 concentration are also verified in this paper. The main contribution of this paper is to develop a deep neural network model that integrates the CNN and LSTM architectures, and through historical data such as cumulated hours of rain, cumulated wind speed and PM2.5 concentration. In the future, this study can also be applied to the prevention and control of PM2.5.

result.paraphrase: Air pollution is a major concern in modern society because it has a severely harmful impact on human health and the environment. Particulate Matter (PM2.5) is an air pollutant made up of suspended particles with diameters of 2.5 μm or less. Its sources include coal-fired power generation, smoke, and dust. These airborne particles can harm the human respiratory and cardiovascular systems, potentially causing illnesses such as asthma, lung cancer, and cardiovascular disease. To monitor and estimate PM2.5 concentration, a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) are combined in a PM2.5 forecasting system. The paper evaluates performance using four metrics: Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Pearson correlation coefficient, and Index of Agreement (IA). Compared with other machine learning methods, the experiments confirm that the proposed CNN-LSTM model (APNet) achieves the highest forecasting accuracy in this paper. The feasibility and practicality of the CNN-LSTM model for predicting PM2.5 concentration are also demonstrated. The paper’s main contribution is developing a deep neural network that integrates CNN and LSTM architectures using historical data such as cumulative rainfall hours, cumulative wind speed, and PM2.5 concentration. In the future, this study may also be used for PM2.5 prevention and control.
